errors.why: The burning-house parable offers distinct carts/vehicles (likely bzhon pa'i khyad par), which is the point of the three-vehicle analogy; glossing them as 'toys' loses that link.

note: Faithful rendering of the Lotus verses, the two parables and the Satyaka-parivarta citation; verse given as prose but without change of sense.

errors.english: You, who possess excellent knowledge, do not desire some specific knowledgeable person.
errors.why: The Tibetan asks the opponent why he does not accept some knower who possesses excellent knowledge; the excellent knowledge belongs to that knower, not to 'you'.

fix.find: You, who possess excellent knowledge, do not desire some specific knowledgeable person.
fix.replace: Why do you not accept some knower who possesses excellent knowledge?

errors.english: they must be certain for one person
errors.why: The objection is that words, being naturally connected to meaning, are restricted to a single meaning, not 'certain for one person'.

fix.find: they must be certain for one person
fix.replace: they must be restricted to a single meaning

errors.english: only those Vedic sounds explain the reality [note: original: kho na nyid]
errors.why: de kho na nyid du here means the Vedic words themselves explain [their meaning] precisely thus and not otherwise; it is not 'reality' (tattva).

note: The argument against self-interpreting Vedic words is followable, but the opening sentence misassigns who has excellent knowledge and the 'fixed to one meaning' objection is misread.

errors.why: bZhin bzang is Sumukha, the haṃsa general of the Jātakamālā story; 'Vadanavara' is an invented Sanskrit name, repeated throughout the page.

note: A faithful and readable rendering of the Haṃsa-jātaka episode; only the general's name is wrong (replace every 'Vadanavara' with 'Sumukha').

errors.why: ci ste here is the lemma 'Now if...' (atha) introducing the anticipated doubt that what is known by the senses exists but not what is known from words, not a question 'Why?'.

errors.english: If it is not like that, but rather because they are realized
errors.why: The Tibetan says 'if because they are cognized otherwise [i.e. later contradicted]', flies etc. in impaired cognition do not exist; the English splits the phrase and loses the argument.

errors.english: yellowish-white [note: original: "ser skya," likely referring to the Samkhya philosophical school's views on qualities]
errors.why: Paired with khra bo (dappled), ser skya is the stock instance-example (tawny vs dappled individual), not a reference to Sāṃkhya.

note: A dense Pramāṇa commentary rendered roughly; the dialectical markers and several lemmas are blurred, and the redundant double glosses obscure rather than help.
Sound rendering of the Vinaya discussion of offending saṅgha members, purification by the jñapti act and the confessable offences; the doubled glosses are clumsy but not wrong.

errors.english: Furthermore, if those individuals one line of text regarding the nature of particulars
errors.why: The side ends with 'Furthermore, if those individuals...'; 'one line of text regarding the nature of particulars' is a stray annotation, not translation.

fix.find: Furthermore, if those individuals one line of text regarding the nature of particulars

note: The universal/particular argument is followed correctly; only a stray editorial phrase at the end needs removing.

errors.english: the inherent nature of the elements as a cause has also been refuted
errors.why: What is refuted is that passion etc. are properties (dharma) of the elements, parallel to their not being properties of wind etc.; nothing is said of the elements 'as a cause'.

fix.find: the inherent nature of the elements as a cause has also been refuted
fix.replace: their being properties of the elements has also been refuted

errors.english: because of the flaw that form and the others are perceived by different sense organs
errors.why: The fault is that form etc. would then be apprehended by a single sense faculty; the English states the true fact instead of the absurd consequence.

fix.find: because of the flaw that form and the others are perceived by different sense organs
fix.replace: because of the flaw that form and the others would be perceived by a single sense organ

errors.english: Furthermore, the basis of support has also been refuted.
errors.why: Both lines are a quoted root verse ('because the support too has been refuted; because it is not the support of the existent or non-existent'); the first is turned into commentary.

note: The anti-materialist argument is mostly followable, but one consequence is reversed and the 'property of the elements' point is misread.

errors.english: This regular order would not exist here.
errors.why: The verse says that this situation (dying though the doṣas are pacified, living though afflicted) would not obtain here [if the body were the cause]; the English presents the first lines as asserted fact and the last as about a 'regular order'.

note: Good rendering of Prajñākaragupta's argument on revival and the doṣas, with the verses kept as verse; one verse is slightly misconstrued.

errors.english: for the purpose of excluding conceptual thought (kalpana) mental fabrication or construction which apprehends a contradictory nature
errors.why: 'Non-erroneous' excludes cognition that is FREE from conceptual construction yet apprehends a contradictory nature (timira etc.); the English drops 'free from' and reverses the point.

fix.find: for the purpose of excluding conceptual thought (kalpana) mental fabrication or construction which apprehends a contradictory nature
fix.replace: for the purpose of excluding cognition free from conceptual construction (kalpanā) which apprehends a contradictory nature

errors.english: to prevent valid cognition (pramana) reliable or valid means of knowledge from becoming erroneous
errors.why: ཚད་མར་འཁྲུལ་པ means mistaking it for a pramāṇa: the purpose is to prevent one from taking that cognition to be valid, not to keep valid cognition from becoming erroneous.

fix.find: to prevent valid cognition (pramana) reliable or valid means of knowledge from becoming erroneous
fix.replace: to prevent its being mistaken for a valid cognition (pramāṇa)

errors.english: Being seated in a boat sentence continues to next page
errors.why: 'sentence continues to next page' is an unmarked editorial remark, not translation.

fix.find: Being seated in a boat sentence continues to next page

note: Readable treatment of 'non-erroneous' and the causes of sensory error, but the key definitional point (excluding non-conceptual error) is reversed.

errors.english: Although it is an aggregation, because it does not transform
errors.why: 'du ba here is samavāya (inherence) of cognition in the self in the Nyāya opponent's view, not 'aggregation'.
In context (next sentence: rtogs pa po) the point is that the self, cognizing, is a cognizer, not that it is 'conceptual'.

note: The refutation of a permanent rememberer is rendered clearly; two terms in the opponent's position are misread.
